say: Put your hand on your chest. That little thump has been going nonstop your whole life, and it never takes a day off.
A healthy adult heart usually beats sixty to a hundred times a minute while you rest. Let's call it about seventy.
Seventy beats a minute adds up fast. By the end of one single day, your heart has beaten about one hundred thousand times.
Keep that going for a whole year and you hit roughly thirty seven million beats. No weekends, no vacation, no snooze button.
Over a long life, that's somewhere around two and a half to three billion heartbeats. Billion, with a B.
Every beat pushes out about four tablespoons of blood. Add it all up and that's around two thousand gallons, every single day.
All that blood rushes through about sixty thousand miles of blood vessels. Laid end to end, they could wrap around Earth twice.
And the wild part? The engine doing all of this is only about the size of your fist, and it weighs less than a pound.
Other animals run at different speeds. An active hummingbird's heart hits about twelve hundred beats a minute, while a diving blue whale's can drop to just two.
So maybe give your heart a little thank you. And follow Simply Weird for more weird stuff like this.
